subject: biology
title: Pathogens and the first line of defence

scenes.heading: Pathogens and the first line of defence
scenes.sub: Why antibiotics won't cure your cold
scenes.say: Every day you breathe in, swallow and touch huge numbers of microorganisms. Most are harmless, but some cause disease. So what are these pathogens, and how does your body keep them out?

scenes.heading: Types of pathogen

right.title: Non-cellular
points: Viruses: nucleic acid in a capsid

scenes.say: A pathogen is any agent that causes disease. Cellular pathogens are Big Friendly Pathogens Who multiply: bacteria, fungi, protozoa and worms. The non-cellular ones are Very Peculiar: viruses and prions. A prion is a bad apple: a misfolded protein that makes normal proteins misfold too.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A food truck has its own kitchen; a recipe on a USB stick doesn't
scenes.science: Bacteria run their own metabolism; viruses must use a host cell
scenes.breaks: a virus isn't a solid object; it's DNA or RNA in a protein coat, and some have a lipid envelope from the host.
scenes.say: A bacterium is like a food truck with its own walls and cooking gear: a cell wall and seventy S ribosomes. A virus is like a recipe on a USB stick. It has to get into a host cell's kitchen to make copies. Antibiotics wreck the food truck, so they do nothing to viruses.

scenes.heading: Self markers: MHC
scenes.say: MHC markers are like school ID lanyards that show who belongs. MHC class one is on all nucleated cells and shows what's going on inside. MHC class two is only on antigen-presenting cells, which hold up pieces of intruders for helper T cells to see.
scenes.caption: MHC markers are like school ID lanyards that show who belongs. MHC class I is on all nucleated cells and shows what's going on inside. MHC class II is only on antigen-presenting cells, which hold up pieces of intruders for helper T cells to see.

scenes.heading: First line: block, burn, bully
scenes.say: The first line of defence is non-specific. Physical barriers block: skin, sticky mucus, and cilia sweeping mucus away. Chemical barriers burn: lysozyme and stomach acid. Microbiological barriers bully: normal flora take all the space and nutrients.

scenes.heading: Plants have barriers too
points: Stomata close when a pathogen is detected
scenes.say: Plants have no circulating immune cells, so barriers matter. They have a waxy cuticle, tough cellulose cell walls and bark. Stomata can close when a pathogen is detected, and plants make antimicrobial chemicals.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: Mice given antibiotics first got sick from Salmonella far more often than mice without. Explain.
scenes.say: Mice given antibiotics got sick from Salmonella more often. Why? Antibiotics killed their normal gut flora. Without that competition for space and nutrients, Salmonella could take hold. The gut flora are a microbiological barrier.

points: MHC I on all nucleated cells; MHC II on APCs
scenes.say: Quick recap. Pathogens can be cellular or non-cellular. MHC markers tell self from non-self. And the first line of defence blocks, burns and bullies pathogens, in both animals and plants. Now try the practice questions!
